approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 5 Chapter 315
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 1962-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the penal law, in relation to enacting "Francesco's
        law";  to amend the executive law, in relation to annual reports
        by the New York state office of  gun  violence  prevention;  and
        providing  for the repeal of certain provisions of the penal law
        relating to safely storing rifles, shotguns, and firearms"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill enacts safe  storage  requirements  for  those  who  possess
firearms,  with  increased  penalties  for  individuals  who leave their
firearm unsecured when they know or reasonably should know  the  firearm
could be accessible to a minor or legally-prohibited person.

  Between  2016  and 2021, suicides accounted for 36% of firearm-related
deaths among children aged 10 to 19. One such child is Francesco, who --
after a campaign of bullying over his sexual orientation -- chose to end
his life with an unsecured firearm. Studies have shown that  individuals
are  less  likely  to  attempt  suicide with a firearm if it is securely
stored and inaccessible. Furthermore, 66% of unintentional fatal firearm
shootings involving children occurred when the firearm was being handled
or shown to someone else.
 
  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature to  address  concerns
regarding  the  safe  harbor  provisions  of the new offenses as well as
reporting requirements in the upcoming legislative session. On the basis
of this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill into law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Enacts "Francesco's law" which establishes violations for the failure to safely store rifles, shotguns, and firearms in the presence of a minor or a prohibited person; requires the office of gun violence prevention to collect and analyze statistical and other information and data with respect to injuries or deaths of minors resulting from failure to safely store a firearm, rifle, or shotgun.
